correctness.rationale: For each finite simple bipartite height-two poset, the primitive-idempotent and arrow Leibniz equations force and permit exactly two arbitrary field coefficients \(b_e,\lambda_e\) per edge. In the vertex/arrow basis the derivation matrix is \([\operatorname{diag}(b)\partial_G\mid\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)]\), so its rank equals \(|L|+|V|-c(V,U)\) after pivoting nonzero lambda rows; the incidence-rank identity is characteristic-independent. Three edge states with weights \(1,q(q-1),q-1\) yield the sum; termwise substitution proves the Tutte identity. Any dependent U contains a graph cycle; shortest such U yields the first rank-shift at girth minus one with multiplicity \(c_g(q-1)^g\). Direct full enumeration of the parameter spaces and solving the entire Leibniz linear system for \(C_4\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\) agreed, but the finite tests are not substituted for general proof. No claim is made about graphs with higher-height posets or all graph-isomorphism classes.

value.rationale: This is the full rank spectrum of the natural derivation representation of a two-level incidence algebra, not an arbitrary matrix invariant or a restatement of derivation-space dimension. It gives a field-uniform exact enumerator for an infinite family and extracts graph girth and the exact number of shortest cycles from algebraic ranks. Those invariants have independent graph-theoretic meaning and are not available merely from the number of derivations. The result gives a testable link between algebra derivations and graphic matroids without requiring a larger downstream theorem.
